scope: Thin native reference adapter over the optional shared KenshikiPulsePassport service; neutral passport and biometric SDKs remain independent.
destinationChanges: The original complete Pulse preparation, wire, registration and verification mechanisms now live once in services/pulse; see services/pulse/provenance.json and governance/architecture/APP-ARCH-001.md A.17.
Use shared KenshikiOperationBinding CanonicalJSON, RegisteredKeyEnrollmentCustody, RegisteredAppAttestSigner and RegisteredKeyAttestationRetryPolicy through the service.
Native adapters retain reader/proof mapping, page correspondence, protected persistence, localization and lifecycle fencing; no legacy identity SDK dependency is linked into reference.
Use a separate reference-app device-only Keychain namespace for registration custody and credentials; no existing Pulse identity is imported.
Preserve exact session/nonce/workflow/operation binding, challenge retirement, bounded responses, truthful failed verdicts and private holder-capability custody.
Retain actual SOD-bound server validation reports; private capability bytes never enter public exports, diagnostics or presentation.
Project actual bounded NFC stage/data-group percentages and explicit transport completion with localized native percent formatting.
Record bounded sanitized diagnostic stages, protocol outcomes, HTTP status and exact allowlisted failure codes; unknown server text is hashed, with credentials and passport content excluded.
Classify exact known server trust-provisioning failures as configuration errors without weakening failed-verdict rejection.
Debug builds record source-bound SOD envelope tags, lengths and exact-fit metadata before submission and on refusal; no passport bytes are exported and verification behavior is unchanged.
validation: Source/protocol tests, native compilation, signed installation and physical chip/server acceptance require separate current receipts.
